note: README has TWO tables. Off-the-shelf table (ViT-S/B/L only, caption 'expected results when using the timm implementation off-the-shelf') contains NO DeiT rows. The DeiT table (DeiT-S/16, DeiT-Ti/16) is TRAINED-with-ToMe and ships checkpoints ('We've trained some DeiT (v1) models using the official implementation'). Therefore no off-the-shelf DeiT-S reference exists in the README. Paper appendix (arXiv:2210.09461) searched (2026-07): Table 11 'Full DeiT Results' (Appendix A.1.4) also gives TRAINED-only numbers ('Results from running a standard 300 epoch DeiT-S ... training run with the official codebase'), including r=8 (79.68), r=13 (79.42 -- differs from the README's 79.36 for the same trained setting; no checkpoint provided for this exact number, likely run-to-run training variance), and r=16 (79.13); no off-the-shelf DeiT-S r-sweep exists anywhere in the paper (main text or appendix). Prior r13 gate vs 79.36 was a setting mismatch (trained ref vs our off-the-shelf run) -- corrected 2026-07.

r0_baseline.setting_verbatim_quote: README DeiT table, column header 'original acc', row 'DeiT-S/16 | 79.8 | 930 | 13 | 79.36 | 1550 | deit_S_r13'. 'original acc' is the checkpoint's own accuracy with NO ToMe merging applied at all -- setting-invariant (true whether merging is later applied post-hoc or trained-in), so directly comparable to our r0 (plain/unpatched) measurement.

off_the_shelf.reason: no published off-the-shelf DeiT-S reference located in README or paper (incl. appendix Table 11, which is trained-only)
off_the_shelf.setting_verbatim_quote: Off-the-shelf table caption: 'Here are some expected results when using the timm implementation off-the-shelf on ImageNet-1k val using a V100:' -- rows are 'ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/16, ViT-L/16 @ 384' only, no DeiT-S row. Paper Table 11 caption: 'Results from running a standard 300 epoch DeiT-S and DeiT-Ti training run with the official codebase on ImageNet-1k' -- trained, not off-the-shelf.
